pain: Agent hits max turns during tool calling
quote: The agent hits MaxTurnsExceeded while executing or chaining tool calls.
text:
Hi everyone,

I’m encountering a MaxTurnsExceeded error while running agents, most frequently during tool calling execution.

Issue description:

The agent hits MaxTurnsExceeded while executing or chaining tool calls.

When this happens, the agent terminates and I’m unable to retrieve the final agent output or the last tool result, even though some work appears to have been completed.

What I’ve tried:

Wrapping execution in a try/except block

Retrying one more tool-calling iteration after catching the exception

However, the same MaxTurnsExceeded exception is raised again, and the output is still not retrievable.

Questions:

What is the root cause of MaxTurnsExceeded in agent tool execution?

Is there a way to retrieve partial or intermediate tool results after this error occurs?

Are there recommended best practices to prevent agents from hitting the max turn limit during tool calls?

pain: Remote MCP tool calls time out on long-running tools
quote: if the tool runs for more than 120 seconds (or even less), it will report error 424
text:
We are using agentbuilder to build workflow. As shown in the following figure, we have added our own remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP) in the agent. But during runtime, we received many 424 errors without any detailed information to explain what exactly caused them.

But the correct result can be obtained by calling it through methods such as curl or fastmcp client.

After multiple debugging attempts, we found that this may be due to the tool running for too long, causing the agent to actively disconnect and report error 424.

We found that if the tool’s runtime is controlled to return results within one minute, the agent can process them normally. But if the tool runs for more than 120 seconds (or even less), it will report error 424.

We are now wondering if there is any way to handle this long-running tool, or if there is any place to adjust the default timeout?

pain: AI Agent tool calls fail or silently return empty results
quote: The AI Agent node itself reports `success` and hands an empty tool result to the model
text:
## Environment

- n8n 2.45.0, self-hosted (Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.45.0`)
- AI Agent node `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` v3.1
- Tool HTTP Request `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest` v1.1
- OpenAI Chat Model `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatOpenAi` v1
- Model endpoint: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the failure happens when the model asks for the tool, before the HTTP request is made)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a Manual Trigger, then an AI Agent node (v3.1).
2. Attach an OpenAI Chat Model as `ai_languageModel`.
3. Attach a Tool HTTP Request (v1.1) as `ai_tool`, with any URL (e.g. `https://example.com`).
4. Give the agent a prompt that makes the model call the tool.
5. Execute the workflow.

## Expected

The tool performs the HTTP request and returns the response body to the agent.

## Actual

The tool node fails with:

```
The node "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest" has a "supplyData" method but no "execute" method.
```

The AI Agent node itself reports `success` and hands an empty tool result to the model, so from the agent's point of view the tool returned nothing. The execution status is `error` only because of the tool node's error.

## Control

The same workflow with the AI Agent node set to v2.2 works: the HTTP request is made and the response (including headers) reaches the model.

So on 2.45.0 `toolHttpRequest` is usable with agent v2.2 and unusable with agent v3.1.

## Additional note

The silent part matters on its own: when a tool fails, the agent does not surface the failure to the model and still finishes `success`. Anyone relying on the model to notice a failed tool call needs to inspect the tool node's `runData` instead.

## Evidence

Local 2.45.0 instance, agent v3.1 workflow:
- execution id 885: `Tool` node `error` with the message above, `Agent` node `success`, agent output `TOOLSAW:""`.
- control execution 890 (agent v2.2, same tool pointed at a closed port): tool node `success` and the model receives `There was an error: "co

pain: Agent memory with tool-call turns breaks the next request
quote: NodeOperationError: messages.0: user messages must have non-empty content
text:
### Bug Description

When a chat session's history contains a turn that was produced via a tool call, the next turn in that same session fails at the AI Agent node (ToolsAgent V3, @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent) with:

NodeOperationError: messages.0: user messages must have non-empty content

Postgres Chat Memory's own loadMemoryVariables output for the same execution shows the prior turn's Human/AI content is fully intact and non-empty at that point. The corruption happens later, inside ToolsAgent V3's own prompt-assembly step, when it flattens buffered memory into the final Anthropic messages[] array — not in memory storage or retrieval.

### To Reproduce

1. Start a fresh chat session. Ask a question that requires a tool call (e.g. a live-data lookup via an HTTP Request Tool node). It succeeds normally.
2. In the same session_id, ask a second question that also requires a tool call.
3. The second turn fails at the AI Agent node with the error above.

### Expected behavior

The agent loads the prior turn from memory and assembles a valid messages[] array for the new request, the same as it does for any session where the prior turn was answered without a tool call.

### Debug Info

Evidence from two real executions in the same production session, ~9 minutes apart, same session_id, same question text:

Execution A (no prior history, fresh session): succeeds.
Execution B (prior history = Execution A's tool-call-derived turn): fails.

Postgres Chat Memory's loadMemoryVariables output for Execution B — non-empty:
{"id":[...,"HumanMessage"],"kwargs":{"data":{"content":"What's today's day-ahead electricity price..."}}}
{"id":[...,"AIMessage"],"kwargs":{"data":{"content":"**Right now (2026-09-26...**..."}}}

The Anthropic Chat Model node's resolved input for the same turn — the equivalent prior-turn slot renders as an empty Human:/AI: placeholder, which reaches the Anthropic API as messages[0] with no content and gets rejected.

Ruled out:
- Storage shape mismatch: stored

pain: Gemini Chat Model fails intermittently inside AI Agent
quote: The Google Gemini Chat Model node intermittently fails when connected to an AI Agent
text: ### Bug Description The Google Gemini Chat Model node intermittently fails when connected to an AI Agent, returning the following error after approximately 3 minutes: ``` [GoogleGenerativeAI Error]: Error fetching from https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite:generateContent: fetch failed Unknown error ``` The issue occurs repeatedly throughout the day. During affected periods, every workflow using an AI Agent connected to Google Gemini Chat Model fails, including newly created test workflows. Interestingly, other methods of accessing the same Gemini API continue working normally during these failures: - **Google Gemini "Message a Model" node:** Works correctly. - **Direct HTTP requests from inside the n8n Docker container:** Work correctly, although sometimes with slightly higher latency. - **AI Agent + OpenAI Chat Model configured with Google's OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoint:** Works correctly, even while the same AI Agent fails using Google Gemini Chat Model. - **AI Agent with OpenRouter using other models:** Works correctly. The most significant finding is that switching only the model node from Google Gemini Chat Model to OpenAI Chat Model, configured to use Google's Gemini API directly, immediately restores functionality without changing the AI Agent itself. The problem persists after updating n8n to the latest available version. This strongly suggests an issue specific to the Google Gemini Chat Model integration, its underlying SDK, or its HTTP connection handling, rather than a general Gemini API outage or network connectivity problem. pain: AI Agent tool calls fail or silently return empty results
quote: intermittently receives an EMPTY observation from a tool call, even though the tool's own execution completes successfully
text:
### Bug Description

n8n version: 2.31.4 (stable)
Nodes: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain Agent (v3.1), toolWorkflow (v2.2), toolCode (v1.3), lmChatOpenAi (v1.3), memoryPostgresChat (v1.4)
Model: gpt-4.1, temperature 0.2

## Summary

An AI Agent node with 4 connected tools (3x toolWorkflow calling sub-workflows, 1x toolCode with inline JS) intermittently receives an EMPTY observation from a tool call, even though the tool's own execution completes successfully and returns the correct data. This causes the agent to either hallucinate plausible-but-fake values, or (with the right system prompt) honestly report "the tool didn't return anything" — both are bad outcomes for a production agent.

## Evidence

With `returnIntermediateSteps: true` on the Agent node, a failing tool call looks like this in `intermediateSteps`:

    "action": { "tool": "get_pricing_info", "toolInput": {...} },
    "observation": "\"\""

Literally the 2-character string `""` — not an error, not null, just an empty JSON string — while the SAME sub-workflow's own execution record (visible separately in n8n's execution log for that nested workflow) shows it computed and returned the correct object via its terminal node, e.g.:

    { "output": "{\"precio_a_mostrar_usd\":100, ...}" }

So the tool itself never fails. The corruption happens strictly in the bridge between the tool node's output and what the LangChain Agent's tool-calling loop reads as the observation.

## What we ruled out (controlled reproduction, ~25 runs across two nearly-identical workflows)

We built a minimal replica workflow (same 4 tools, same sub-workflows, same LLM/credential) alongside the real one, and isolated variables one at a time. None of these reproduced the bug in the replica, even though the SAME exact payload reliably reproduced it on the real workflow:

- Tool type (toolCode vs. simple toolWorkflow vs. complex toolWorkflow with a 25-node sub-workflow)
- Calling 1 tool vs. calling all 4 sequentially in a single turn
- Chat
